Business in Minneapolis

When everyone is good, specific wins.

In a city this size, your customer has a dozen good options within a few miles. Being good is the minimum. The business that gets chosen is the one that says exactly who it is for, so the right person recognizes themselves straight away.

That is a positioning decision, not a design one, and it is the step most Minneapolis businesses skip on the way to a new logo. It is the first thing we do.

Also working with businesses in Northeast, North Loop, Uptown, Edina and Saint Louis Park.

  • Sounding like everyone else

    If your website could swap names with a competitor’s and nobody would notice, the problem is the message, not the colors.

  • Too broad to be remembered

    Serving everyone in the metro means nobody thinks of you first. Narrowing feels risky, and it is what makes you the first name someone thinks of.

  • Paying for design before decisions

    A rebrand without positioning is an expensive way to look different and say the same thing.

The Strategy Day

One day to decide.

For the business that needs a decision more than a build. We work through four things in order, and by the end of the day the hardest questions about your brand have answers, in writing.

  1. Audit

    What is working, what is not, and why: your website, your offers, your reviews and how you describe the business today.

  2. Discovery

    Who you serve best, who you want more of, and what they are choosing between when they find you.

  3. Positioning

    The one clear decision: who the business is for and what it should be known for.

  4. Message

    The words to say it, on your website, in a conversation and in a search result.

Questions

Before you book.

Something not here? Ask me directly. I answer every one myself.

Do you work with Minneapolis businesses in person?

Yes. I’m based in Forest Lake, north of the cities, and I meet Minneapolis clients in person or remotely, whichever suits the work.

How is this different from hiring a Minneapolis branding agency?

An agency hands you a project and moves on. I’m one person across brand, operations and business development, and I stay in the work after launch. The Strategy Day is where that starts.

How much does brand strategy cost?

A Strategy Day is $1,500, flat, with no hourly add-ons. If you go on to a website, that starts at $4,000, and a Full Brand Launch starts at $15,000.

Can you help with a rebrand?

Yes, and a rebrand is where a Strategy Day matters most. We decide what has to change, and what has earned the right to stay, before anyone touches the logo.
